definition.falsification: If preferences remain uniformly distributed regardless of accumulated memory sequences or if stability scores fall significantly below 0.9 under varied reinforcement sequences, the hypothesis is falsified.
definition.statement: Accumulated memory sequences generate distinct, stable preference configurations under reinforcement mechanisms.
definition.uncertainty: The mapping between specific memory sequence structure and long-term preference stability is not fully characterized.

definition.method: Execute a reinforced path-dependency simulation with variable input orderings to test sensitivity of preference outcomes to memory sequence structure.
definition.success: Consistency of output measurements across varied memory sequence inputs.
